script: Where should the final of the 2030 World Cup be played? The 2030 World Cup is being co-hosted by Spain, Portugal, and Morocco, and right now Spain and Morocco are in a serious tug of war over who gets the final. Morocco is spending around half a billion dollars on a brand new stadium outside Casablanca that will hold 115,000 people, making it the biggest football stadium in the world, and their architect literally said it was designed and made for the 2030 final. Spain fired back through their federation president, Rafael Louzán, who said it would be inexplicable if the final wasn't held in Spain, at the Santiago Bernabéu or Camp Nou. But Spain isn't leaning on stadium size to win this, and their real angle is far bolder. Louzán says Spain carries 55% organizational weight of this whole tournament and that the World Cup was basically born as a Spain and Portugal bid with Morocco joining later. So since he's hosting the most matches, he feels the final should follow the weight. Morocco's side just points at the numbers, because their stadium is bigger than anything Spain has, and a final in Casablanca would be only the second time in history that an African city hosts a World Cup final. But once you look at FIFA's own rulebook, you realize why neither side can actually prove they're right. FIFA has published exactly how it evaluates stadiums for capacity and safety, yet it has never published a single rule for how it picks the stadium that hosts the final. So FIFA informally decides the final through technical checks, private consultation with the host countries, and ultimately its own discretion.
